deep_dive.title: Exact Quantile Balancing and Load-Error Injection for Mixture-of-Experts
deep_dive.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) training requires global load balance to prevent expert under-utilization and local balance for efficient expert-parallel execution. Existing distributed Quantile Balancing (QB) uses shard-dependent or approximate global quantiles, while token-independent expert biases cannot ensure microbatch-level balance. We introduce Exact Quantile Balancing (EQB), which computes exact global-batch BF16 quantiles with negligible communication, and Load-Error Injection (LEI), which injects local load errors directly into router-score gradients. On 7.5B-parameter MoEs trained for up to 500B tokens, EQB improves global balance and downstream performance over naive QB, while LEI improves local balance and outperforms the GShard loss at comparable quality.

deep_dive.llm_tldr_en: MoE training needs global and local load balance. The authors propose Exact Quantile Balancing (exact global BF16 quantiles) and Load-Error Injection (local load errors into router-score gradients), improving balance and downstream performance on 7.5B MoEs trained up to 500B tokens.
deep_dive.llm_tldr_cn: 混合专家训练需要全局负载均衡以避免专家利用不足，同时需要局部均衡以支持高效专家并行。本文提出精确分位均衡EQB，以极低通信开销计算精确的全局批次BF16分位，并提出负载误差注入LEI，把局部负载误差直接注入路由分数的梯度中。在7.5B参数、训练至500B token的MoE上，EQB改善了全局均衡与下游性能，LEI改善了局部均衡并优于GShard损失。该工作为MoE路由的均衡训练提供了更精确且可扩展的方案。

quick_skim.title: SSD-LLaMA: SSD-Native Inference for Trillion-Parameter MoE at 1+ Token/s on a Consumer PC
quick_skim.abstract: Frontier open-weight language models increasingly use Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures to expand model capacity while activating only a small subset of experts per token. Local inference must nevertheless keep the complete expert pool available, which remains far beyond consumer-grade RAM and VRAM capacity even after quantization. SSDs provide practical capacity at this scale, but turning that capacity into executable model memory requires efficient expert delivery, coordinated management of SSD, RAM, and VRAM, and CPU--GPU hybrid execution under bounded bandwidth. We present \textit{SSD-LLaMA}, an SSD-native local MoE inference system that addresses these challenges with an SSD I/O pipeline optimized for expert delivery, a native three-tier storage hierarchy that delivers and retains experts dynamically, and balanced CPU--GPU hybrid execution. \textit{SSD-LLaMA} executes every selected expert without pruning or substitution. Across three frontier MoE model families, \textit{SSD-LLaMA} improves prefill token rate by 1.52$\times$--4.19$\times$ and decode token rate by 2.10$\times$--15.58$\times$ over the evaluated baselines. We also achieve higher than 1 token/s for running trillion-parameter model with a single RTX 5090 and no more than 32GB RAM.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: Frontier MoE models activate few experts per token but need the full expert pool resident. The authors present SSD-LLaMA, an SSD-native local MoE inference system with an expert-delivery I/O pipeline and coordinated SSD-RAM-VRAM management, achieving 1+ token/s on a consumer PC.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 前沿开源大模型越来越多采用混合专家架构以扩大容量同时仅激活少量专家，但本地推理仍需保留完整专家池，超出消费级内存与显存容量。本文提出SSD-LLaMA，一种SSD原生的本地MoE推理系统，设计了面向专家传输优化的SSD I/O流水线，并协调SSD、内存与显存管理及CPU-GPU混合执行。该系统在消费级PC上实现每秒超过1个token的万亿参数MoE推理。该工作从系统层面推进了MoE模型的本地可部署性。

quick_skim.title: Hunyuan-A13B Technical Report
quick_skim.abstract: We present Hunyuan-A13B, an open-source large language model based on a Mixture-of-Experts architecture. It contains 80 billion total parameters but activates only 13 billion during inference, balancing model capability, computational efficiency, and deployment cost. The model is pretrained on a rigorously filtered 20T-token corpus with enhanced STEM data curation, improving factual reliability and reasoning ability. High-quality supervised fine-tuning and large-scale reinforcement learning further enhance its overall performance. Hunyuan-A13B also introduces a dual-mode Chain-of-Thought framework that adapts reasoning depth to task complexity: fast thinking for routine queries and slow thinking for complex, multi-step problems. Evaluations show competitive performance across mathematics, science, programming, general language understanding, and agent tasks, often approaching that of much larger models. Its high inference throughput makes it suitable for latency-sensitive applications. We release Hunyuan-A13B to support open research and practical LLM deployment.
